Byomkesh.description: The protagonist, a renowned Bengali detective known as a 'truth-seeker' (satyanweshi), who investigates complex cases with keen observation and logic.

Pandeyji.description: A senior police officer and friend of Byomkesh, who assists in the investigation and provides local insight.

Ratikanta.description: Inspector Ratikanta Chowdhury, a young police officer, relative of Dipnarayan Singh, and involved in the official investigation.

Dipnarayan Singh.description: A wealthy and influential zamindar of Bihar, recently recovered from illness, who becomes the murder victim.

Dr. Palit.description: A Bengali physician responsible for treating Dipnarayan Singh, who administers the fatal injection.

Dr. Jagannath Prasad.description: A young Bihari doctor, nicknamed 'Ghoda Jagannath' (Horse Jagannath), known for his arrogance and rivalry with Bengali doctors.

Debnarayan.description: Dipnarayan Singh's obese and foolish nephew, who stands to inherit the estate.

Beniprasad.description: Debnarayan's close companion and jester, known for his wit.

Liladhar Banshi.description: Assistant manager of the estate and Debnarayan's assistant jester.

Gangadhar Banshi.description: Chief manager of Dipnarayan Singh's estate and father of Liladhar, described as a shrewd and enigmatic figure.

Shakuntala.description: Dipnarayan Singh's beautiful and accomplished young wife, skilled in the arts and a graduate of Allahabad University.

Chandni.description: Debnarayan's wife, depicted as plump, shy, and unaccustomed to socializing openly.

Miss Manna.description: The resident lady doctor of the house, called to attend to Shakuntala after Dipnarayan's death.

Khublal.description: Dr. Palit's compounder, a poor Bihari assistant who is questioned during the investigation.

Narmada Shankar.description: A notorious, wealthy young man from Allahabad, known for his scandalous behavior and former visitor to Dipnarayan's house.

Calcutta.description: A major city in eastern India (now Kolkata), referenced as the origin of Byomkesh and his friends.

Bihar.description: An Indian state where the story is set, known for its zamindari estates and conservative social customs.

Pratapgarh.description: A region in India, mentioned as the ancestral home of Ratikanta's family.

Allahabad University.description: A prestigious university in Allahabad (now Prayagraj), India, from which Shakuntala graduated.

Patna.description: The capital city of Bihar, where much of the story's action occurs.

Buxar.description: A town in Bihar, referenced as the location of a jail.

Ganges.description: A major river in India, referenced metaphorically as a 'one-way journey' (i.e., death).

hookah.description: A traditional Indian water pipe used for smoking tobacco.

sahib.description: A term of respect used in colonial India for Europeans or people of high status.

zamindar.description: A hereditary landowner or landlord, especially in pre-independence India.

purdah.description: The practice of secluding women from public observation, prevalent in some Indian households.

adda.description: An informal gathering or conversation, often among friends, typical in Bengali culture.

baithak-khana.description: A sitting room or drawing room in an Indian household.

paṭaṅga.description: A word meaning 'moth' in Hindi/Bengali, used in the story's title.

huzoor.description: A respectful form of address, meaning 'sir' or 'master' in Urdu/Hindi.

compounder.description: A medical assistant responsible for preparing and dispensing medicines in a clinic.

bandhgala.description: A formal Indian jacket, typically worn by men.

paan.description: A preparation of betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, chewed as a stimulant.

sari.description: A traditional Indian garment worn by women, consisting of a long piece of cloth draped around the body.

B.Sc..description: Bachelor of Science, an undergraduate academic degree.

civil marriage.description: A marriage performed and recognized by the state, not based on religious rites.

curare.description: A plant-derived poison used historically on arrow tips and referenced here as a means of murder.

post-mortem.description: An autopsy; the examination of a body after death to determine the cause.

intramuscular.description: A type of injection administered into a muscle.

satyanweshi.description: A term meaning 'truth-seeker', used to describe Byomkesh's approach to detection.
